items.why: The 1916 probate calendar (p.301) records a grant of probate, not administration, so a will existed and was proved. items.title: Thomas v Hurst (1812-1813): the Chancery decree, the Master's report naming the buyers, and the sale particulars with their lot plan for the Llandough-juxta-Penarth freeholds

They would show who held the Llandough-juxta-Penarth land before the Bute estate's record of the farm begins in 1824. items.title: Tithe redemption annuity records for the holding's tithe plots, 1936-1977: whom the Crown treated as fee-simple owner
items.holder: The National Archives, Kew: IR 94/51/58 and IR 90/51/58 (catalogued; originals not digitised, not viewed). Any annuities register or owner notice for the district: whereabouts not known.
items.basis: statute (Tithe Act 1936 ss.3(1), 16(1), 17(1), 18; Tithe Act 1951 s.1) + cross-reference (The National Archives catalogue: IR 94/51/58, IR 90/51/58; IR 29/51/58 apportionment copy)
items.why: The Tithe Act 1936 extinguished each tithe rentcharge and replaced it with a redemption annuity charged in respect of the land on which the rentcharge had been charged (s.3(1)). Each instalment was made a debt due to the Crown from the person who, on the due date, was the owner of that land (s.16(1)), and 'owner' meant the estate owner in respect of the fee simple, or a lessee for a long term at less than a rack rent (s.17(1)). The Tithe Redemption Commission could serve a person as owner for the annuities register, and a person served could deny ownership, leaving a court to decide (s.18). In the c.1841 apportionment the holding's plots carried a rentcharge of 11 pounds 13s 1d. The Commission's papers for this district should therefore show whom the Crown treated, and billed, as fee-simple owner of those plots from 1936, across the 1938 conveyance, from a source outside the estate's own deeds. Against: the Tithe Act 1951 (s.1) ended the duty to prepare a register for every district, so an owner register for Llandough may never have been made; the IR 94 orders exist only where a plot was later apportioned, and whether IR 94/51/58 or IR 90/51/58 touch the holding's plots is not checked; remaining annuities were ended in 1977 (not checked against the enacted text here). Parcel not identified (the holding's c.1841 plots lie within tithe 196-267 and 275-281; the order or register entry itself would name the plots).

items.title: Deposited plans and books of reference for the railway and waterworks schemes over Llandough, 1876-1901: owner, lessee and occupier of each plot
items.holder: Parliamentary Archives deposited plans, catalogued in The National Archives' Discovery: YHL/PO/PB/3/plan1876/P4 (Penarth Extension Railway), YHL/PO/PB/3/plan1885/B4 and plan1884/B5 (Barry Dock and Railways; which file carries Railway No.1 not checked), YHL/PO/PB/3/plan1897/T1, plan1900/T5 and plan1901/T2 (Taff Vale Railway); House of Commons copies under YHC/CL/PB/6. No catalogue entry located for the 1893 Cardiff Corporation waterworks deposit. The county deposits with the clerk of the peace (Glamorgan Quarter Sessions): whether held at Glamorgan Archives not checked.
items.basis: practice required by Parliament's standing orders for private Bills (deposit of plans, sections and books of reference; Gazette notice; list of owners, lessees and occupiers) + statute (Lands Clauses Consolidation Act 1845, incorporated in the Bills) + cross-reference (London Gazette issues 25417 p.5380, 26460 p.6693, 26797 p.6654, 27380 p.8304; The National Archives catalogue entries for the Parliament Office deposited-plan series)
items.why: Every private Bill seeking compulsory powers over land had to deposit, before the session, a plan of the lands and a book of reference naming the owner, lessee and occupier of every numbered plot, with Parliament and with the clerk of the peace of the county; the Gazette notice and a list of owners, lessees and occupiers (showing who assented, dissented or stayed neutral) followed. Notices in the London Gazette show at least four schemes with powers over land in Llandough-juxta-Cardiff: the Penarth Extension Railway (1876); the Barry Dock and Railways Company's Railway No.1, ending in Llandough by a junction with the Penarth Extension, with the Lands Clauses Acts incorporated (notice of 25 November 1884); Cardiff Corporation's waterworks conduit from the Cogan reservoir, ending in Llandough (notice of 21 November 1893); and the Taff Vale Railway's Bill of 1896 for compulsory purchase of lands in Llandough east of the Penarth branch near Llandough Lower Junction, whose 1897 Act authorised compulsory purchase of plots numbered 13-18, 21 and 22 on the deposited plans in that parish, with time extended in 1900 and again sought in 1901. The books of reference for these schemes should therefore name, plot by plot, who was treated as owner and who as occupier of every piece of land the schemes touched in the parish, from a source outside the estate's own papers. Against: a book of reference records the owner of record and the occupier as the promoters found them, so for land of the Bute estate it would be expected to show the estate as owner and any farmer as occupier; deposited-plan numbers are not tithe numbers, and whether any listed plot lies within the holding is not checked; a scheme deposited is not a scheme built, and land named in a book of reference was not always taken. Parcel not identified (the holding's c.1841 plots lie within tithe 196-267 and 275-281; the deposited plan for each scheme would show whether any of its plots fall within them).

items.title: Superfluous-land records for land taken in Llandough under the Lands Clauses Acts: to whom any surplus was offered back, and when
items.holder: The railway companies' land and estate papers: Barry Railway Company (The National Archives RAIL 23) and Taff Vale Railway Company (RAIL 684), with any later successor estate files; Cardiff Corporation waterworks land papers (Cardiff Council / Glamorgan Archives, not checked). Not yet searched item by item.
items.basis: statute (Lands Clauses Consolidation Act 1845, ss.127-128, incorporated in the Barry Dock and Railways, Taff Vale Railway and Cardiff Corporation Bills) + cross-reference (London Gazette notices of 1884, 1893, 1896 and 1901; The National Archives series RAIL 23 and RAIL 684)
items.why: Where a company took land under the Lands Clauses Consolidation Act 1845 and did not need all of it for its works, the Act required it to sell the superfluous land within a fixed period after the time for completing the works, and first to offer it to the person then entitled to the land from which it was taken, or failing that to the owners of adjoining land (ss.127-128). The railway and waterworks schemes with powers over Llandough-juxta-Cardiff incorporated the Lands Clauses Acts. A company that sold or offered back surplus land in the parish should therefore have left a record of the offer, the person it was made to and the answer: the offer-back rule is the nineteenth-century forerunner of the arrangements later named after Crichel Down. Against: the offer went to the person entitled to the land, that is the owner of record, or to adjoining owners, not to an occupier or tenant, so for land of the Bute estate an offer would be expected to go to the estate; the rule did not apply to land kept for the works, and whether any Llandough land was ever treated as superfluous is not checked; the company records may survive only in part. Parcel not identified (the conveyances and land plans would name the plots).

items.title: Building preservation notice for the farmhouse in 1988, or the council's record of deciding not to serve one
items.holder: Vale of Glamorgan Council (planning records of the former borough council, 1988), and South Glamorgan County Council papers at Glamorgan Archives; the occupier's own papers if a notice was served. Not yet searched.
items.basis: statute (Town and Country Planning Act 1971 s.58(1), (3) and (5), as enacted) + cross-reference (Cadw resurvey 29 Jul 1988; spot-listing refused 5 Dec 1988; demolition 6 Dec 1988)
items.why: Between the Cadw resurvey visit of 29 July 1988 and the refusal to spot-list on 5 December 1988, the farmhouse (Parcel A, the house) was an unlisted building whose interest had been put to the Secretary of State. Section 58 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971 let the local planning authority protect such a building at once, for six months, by serving a building preservation notice 'on the owner and occupier of the building'. The notice had to state that the authority had asked the Secretary of State to consider listing it. If one was served and the Secretary of State then declined to list, s.58(5)(a) required the authority to 'forthwith give notice of the Secretary of State's decision to the owner and occupier'. So if a notice was served there should be two papers, each served on the occupier as well as the registered proprietor: the notice itself and the later notice of the decision. If none was served, the council's planning file or committee papers for late 1988 are where a decision not to use the power would be written down. Against: the power was discretionary and nothing required a record of a decision not to use it; a notice could be costly for the authority if the building was not then listed, which made councils cautious; and once the Secretary of State had declined to list on 5 December, a notice would have ended at once. Section 58 is read here as enacted in 1971; amendments up to 1988, and whether the county or the district council held the power for this building, are not checked.

items.title: 1910 Finance Act valuation record sheet plans for Llandough, the maps that pair with the Glamorgan Archives valuation book DVAL/1/33
items.holder: The National Archives, Kew: IR 131/4 (Cardiff District record sheet plans). The valuation book DVAL/1/33 is at Glamorgan Archives.
items.basis: cross-reference (Glamorgan Archives reply of 7 Sep 2026 naming the Llandough valuation book DVAL/1/33 and stating that the maps are held by The National Archives; TNA Discovery, series IR 131/4 'Finance Act 1910, Record Sheet Plans: Welsh Region: Cardiff District', read 8 Nov 2026); statute (Finance (1909–10) Act 1910, land valuation); the Glamorgan Archives catalogue entry for DVAL/1/33 is not checked (the catalogue did not load)
items.why: DVAL/1/33 is not a reference at The National Archives. It is Glamorgan Archives' reference for the 1910 land valuation book for Llandough; Glamorgan Archives wrote on 7 Sep 2026 that it does not hold the maps that go with the book and that they are at The National Archives. The maps that pair with it are the Finance Act 1910 record sheet plans for the Cardiff valuation district, series IR 131/4, one 1:2500 Ordnance Survey sheet per piece. The assessment numbers marked on those sheets tie each plot to its entry in the valuation book and in the field books (IR 58). For Great House the sheet is Glamorgan XLVII.6, IR 131/4/96, already recorded on MR-0048. Other Glamorgan XLVII sheets in the same series that may cover the rest of the parish: XLVII.2 (IR 131/4/94), XLVII.3 (IR 131/4/54), XLVII.5 (IR 131/4/95), XLVII.7 (IR 131/4/97; Penarth quarters IR 131/4/245 and 246), XLVII.10 (IR 131/4/99) and XLVII.11 (Penarth quarters IR 131/4/247 to 249). Which of these the parish covers is not checked. Against: the sheets show plot boundaries and assessment numbers only; the owner, occupier and tenure are in the book and the field books.

items.title: The applicant's copy of the list of documents delivered with the February 1983 first-registration application for the farmhouse and garden (title WA240304)
items.holder: The applicant's side: the deed records of BP Properties Ltd and its successors, or the solicitors who lodged the 1983 application. The Registry's copy is MR-0020.
items.basis: statute (Land Registration Rules 1925, r.20(i)-(iv), text read in a c.1930 printing of the rules); cross-reference (HM Land Registry document list for WA240304, 30 Jul 2026; MR-0020); practice (return of deeds with the applicant's copy, not checked)
items.why: Rule 20 of the Land Registration Rules 1925, as printed in a statute collection of about 1930, required an application for first registration to be accompanied by every original deed and document relating to the title in the applicant's possession or control (abstracts of title, contracts and counsel's opinions included), a copy or abstract of the latest document of title, particulars by plan, and 'a list in triplicate of all documents delivered'. The application for the farmhouse and garden (WA240304) was made by BP Properties Ltd on 23 February 1983. A list in three copies should therefore have existed, and in ordinary conveyancing practice one copy comes back to the applicant's solicitors with the returned deeds (practice, not checked for this file). That list would show which documents BP Properties Ltd showed as its title: the May 1975 conveyance (MR-0050), and whether the 1938 conveyance, the 1969 conveyance or any abstract went in. The Registry's own copy and examination papers are MR-0020; the Registry's document list of 30 July 2026 keeps only the 1975 conveyance and plans for this title. Against: the rule allowed the Registrar to direct otherwise; amendments to rule 20 between 1930 and 1983 are not checked; a list that does not survive is a records gap, not evidence of anything done wrong.

items.title: Glamorgan County Naturalists' Trust site files, survey records, maps and photographs for Llandough and Leckwith, 1961–2002
items.status: NOT HELD BY THE WILDLIFE TRUST; POSSIBLE COPIES AT SEWBREC, NOT YET ASKED
items.holder: South East Wales Biodiversity Records Centre (digitised Mary Gillham archive), not yet asked. The Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales holds nothing in the office (reply of 7 Nov 2026).
items.basis: practice (county naturalists' trust site files and survey records, 1961–2002); cross-reference (SSSI 0524 notification, MR-0083; the Trust's reply of 7 Nov 2026 pointing to the Mary Gillham archive at SEWBReC)
items.why: The Glamorgan County Naturalists' Trust, founded in January 1961 and later the Glamorgan Wildlife Trust, merged into the present Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales in 2002. A county naturalists' trust of that period kept site files and survey notes on woodland and grassland it watched or proposed for protection, and the wooded slopes between Llandough and Leckwith were notified as an SSSI (0524) in the same years (MR-0083). Such files would record who was approached as owner or occupier of the land, a third party's contemporary account of who held and worked it. On 7 Nov 2026 the Trust replied that it does not hold any data on the site, that it 'may have had some historically', and that some of the paperwork was lost in a fire in about 2003; it pointed to the digitised archive of the naturalist Mary Gillham, held by the South East Wales Biodiversity Records Centre (SEWBReC), as the most likely home of anything that survived. Against: the Trust could not say any file on this site ever existed; a naturalist's survey report would describe habitat and species, not tenure, and may not name the farm. Parcel not identified: the woodland (Parcel A woodland) and the Leckwith slopes are the likely subjects; a grid reference or site name in a surviving report would identify it.
